claim: Morphological grades of blastocyst development stage, ICM, and TE have shown limited predictive power on clinical outcomes.
source: While the blastocyst morphological grading is widely used in clinical practice, morphological grades of the development stage, ICM, and TE have shown limited predictive power on clinical outcomes (Seli et al., 2011; Reignier et al., 2019; Bartolacci et al., 2021; Ueno et al., 2021; Xiong et al., 2022).

claim: CNN is able to automatically detect discriminative features from images.
source: CNN is able to automatically detect discriminative features from images and has been the state-of-the-art method in various fields in medical imaging, such as lung cancer prediction (Ardila et al., 2019), breast cancer prediction (McKinney et al., 2020), and diabetic retinopathy screening (Bora et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to applications in lung cancer (Ardila et al., 2019), breast cancer (McKinney et al., 2020), and diabetic retinopathy (Bora et al., 2021)

claim: AUCs reported in the literature using CNN to predict clinical outcomes from blastocyst images range from 0.64 to 0.71 for pregnancy prediction.
source: The AUCs reported in the literature using CNN to predict clinical outcomes from blastocyst images range from 0.64 to 0.71 for pregnancy prediction (VerMilyea et al., 2020; Kragh et al., 2021b; Berntsen et al., 2022; Enatsu et al., 2022; Loewke et al., 2022), and are around 0.65 for live birth prediction (Miyagi et al., 2019; Nagaya and Ukita, 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to VerMilyea et al., 2020; Kragh et al., 2021b; Berntsen et al., 2022; Enatsu et al., 2022; Loewke et al., 2022

claim: AUCs reported in the literature using CNN are around 0.65 for live birth prediction.

evidence: Supported by citations to Miyagi et al., 2019; Nagaya and Ukita, 2021

claim: CNN using static images achieved similar or slightly better accuracies in predicting clinical outcomes than using time-lapse videos.
source: However, results in the literature show that CNN using static images achieved similar or slightly better accuracies in predicting clinical outcomes than using time-lapse videos, for instance, AUC=0.68–0.71 (VerMilyea et al., 2020; Enatsu et al., 2022; Loewke et al., 2022) versus 0.64–0.67 (Kragh et al., 2021b; Berntsen et al., 2022) for pregnancy prediction, and 0.66 (Miyagi et al., 2019) versus 0.65 (Nagaya and Ukita, 2021) for live birth prediction.
evidence: Supported by citations comparing static images (VerMilyea et al., 2020; Enatsu et al., 2022; Loewke et al., 2022; Miyagi et al., 2019) versus time-lapse videos (Kragh et al., 2021b; Berntsen et al., 2022; Nagaya and Ukita, 2021)
